**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Attempting to add ResourceVersion precondition to
eviction requests results in a conflict failure. This
is due to the fact that we apply a deletion timestamp
which mutates the underlying resource.  The resource
version is then checked again later in the code.

This commit removes the ResourceVersion precondition
after the object has a deletion timestamp applied.

issue_context.title: Graceful deletion mutates object invalidating ResourceVersion in deletion precondition
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

When developing unit tests related to PDBs/Deletion,https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/generic/registry/store.go#L932 mutates pod resource via adding deletion timestamp, and this directly conflicts with checking resource version.

**What you expected to happen**:

No resource version mutation.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I'm attempting to add preconditions to delete call in eviction API:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83906/files#diff-9644c646d1076728c605baed12a5813aR138



**Anything else we need to know?**:
Happens locally and in CI.

> When developing unit tests related to PDBs/Deletion, k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go:conditionalDelete mutates pod resource version when it shouldn't.

can you provide more details about what you're observing?

@liggitt 

You can see an example here: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/83906/pull-kubernetes-bazel-test/1197243638665449474

```
     --- FAIL: TestEviction/matching_pdbs_with_no_disruptions_allowed,_pod_pending (0.16s)
        eviction_test.go:176: expected error=false, got Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods "t2": StorageError: invalid object, Code: 4, Key: /registry/pods/default/t2, ResourceVersion: 0, AdditionalErrorMsg: Precondition failed: ResourceVersion in precondition: 2, ResourceVersion in object meta: 3; name t2 
```

Here's the relevant section of the tests:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eb83891d5fe585030fcb2cb89deda86b6dc8a3f/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction_test.go#L145



There really shouldn't be anything modifying the pod after creation until the delete request, thus I don't believe we should be hitting this precondition failure.  Resource Version in precondition I believe to be correct, but when we contact etcd to verify, it's increased by one.  It's not clear why this is happening, it appears to be a bug.

Okay, I've sorted this out.  We have a conflict with 'graceful' deletion with this approach:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/generic/registry/store.go#L932

This updates the object to add a deletion timestamp, thus the first call to eviction will always fail if we need to set ResourceVersion.

review_comments: if `preconditions.ResourceVersion` is set, that also means `options.Preconditions.ResourceVersion` is set, right? do we need to update that as well? if so, do we need to copy delete options first to avoid mutating what was passed in?

We don't need to copy delete options, we don't pass it anywhere, it dead-ends in this function and we access the variables directly as we need them (we set preconditions earlier in the function and never refer to the ones in options again).

With the test I've added we should be safe against regression.  Delete options is specifically for this function, so not sure what the benefit of copying would be at this time.
got it, I misread the later use of `options.DryRun` and thought we were passing the entire options struct into subcalls
did this test fail before the fix?

This behavior was not tested before the fix.  If you comment out the code I added in store.go, you'll see this test fail in the covered case.  Also, if you look at my PR test history for the eviction PR, you'll see it failing there before this fix went in.
